clue.text: Defender defending header from Leeds player

indicators.note: a header is the top of something, so only the opening letter of the word is taken
to defend is to shield on all sides, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: a back is a defensive player in football
the first letter of Leeds

explanation.surface: A defender clears the ball with his head away from a Leeds United forward.
explanation.walkthrough: The football surface makes 'player' look like another footballer, but it is a chess player: the side with the dark pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the two opponents are called white and black, after the colour of the pieces each moves.

clue.text: Bishop first to admit sex is a temptation

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the first letter of admit
'it' is a coy word for sex, as in 'doing it'

explanation.surface: A clergyman confesses that sex tempts him.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex is an old crossword standby, from the euphemism in phrases such as 'they were at it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bait is something offered to lure or entice, so it is a synonym for a temptation or enticement.

clue.text: A saucy artist enthralling you with line of crack?

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so one piece holds another inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
pert means cheeky or saucy
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
U is text-speak for you
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A cheeky painter draws you in with a cheap line about cracks, in the rude sense.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is a standard crossword artist. The question mark flags that 'of crack' is an unusual way to define an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Apertural is the adjective from aperture, an opening or gap, so it describes something relating to a crack.

clue.text: Winger appearing in Nike advertisements

indicators.note: something appearing in words sits inside them, visible across the join

blocks.note: found spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A football winger stars in adverts for Nike boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' sounds like a footballer in a sportswear ad, but here it is anything with wings: a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The kea is a large mountain parrot of New Zealand, and any bird can be called a winger in crosswords.

clue.text: Complex Irishman returning service off the net?

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so these letters are read backwards

blocks.note: a web is a complex network, as in a web of lies
Liam is a common Irish man's name

explanation.surface: A complicated Irish tennis player returns a serve that clips the net.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis words 'returning service' and 'net' are all misdirection: service is an email service and the net is the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Webmail is email accessed through a browser, a service delivered from the internet.

clue.text: Pure smack that you and I must pick up

indicators.note: to pick something up is to take it into your hands, so one piece gathers another inside

blocks.note: you and I together are we
to smack is to hit

explanation.surface: A drug user talks about buying uncut heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: Smack is slang for heroin, and 'pick up' sounds like scoring drugs, but smack is simply a blow here.
explanation.definitionFit: White is the colour of purity and innocence, so it stands for clean or unsullied.

clue.text: Give a whipping to a bad English citizen abroad

indicators.note: a thrashing knocks something about, so its letters end up in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rework

explanation.surface: Someone wants a badly behaved English expat flogged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' is part of the definition, not an anagram signal: the citizen is of a foreign country.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bangladeshi is a national of Bangladesh, a country outside Britain, so a citizen from overseas.

clue.text: Everybody with any hope at front will find God

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only those are kept

blocks.note: everybody is all
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Anyone who keeps hope foremost will find God, a line from a sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At front' applies to both 'any' and 'hope', so each gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Allah is the Arabic name for God, used by Muslims and Arabic-speaking Christians alike.

clue.text: City financier involved in decreases in value

indicators.note: something involved in a thing is caught up inside it

blocks.note: a share that loses has fallen in value
an angel is a backer who finances a venture, often a theatre show

explanation.surface: A City of London money man is mixed up in falling share prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' at the start suggests the London financial district, but it is simply the definition. Angel for a backer is common in theatre and start-up funding.
explanation.definitionFit: Los Angeles is the large Californian city, home of Hollywood.

clue.text: The learned and I will mess around with it later

indicators.note: to mess around with something is to fiddle with it until it is in disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone says the academics and they will tinker with the thing afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the front; 'and' and 'will' only join it to the jumbled letters of I, IT and LATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Literati are educated people interested in literature, so the learned as a group.

clue.text: Don't you know numbers the French burst into?

indicators.note: bursting into a place means ending up inside it

blocks.note: NOS is the abbreviation for numbers
les is French for 'the' in the plural

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you know the songs a French crowd broke into.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hides that the definition is a whole phrase used for emphasis.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are tag phrases stressing something impressive: 'he met the Queen, no less' matches 'he met the Queen, don't you know'.

clue.text: Let a night with her set in motion true love!

indicators.note: setting something in motion stirs it about, so the letters move into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A romantic urges that one night with her will start genuine love.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark belongs to the surface; every letter of 'Let a night' and 'her' is used once.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used of genuine, lasting love as opposed to infatuation, as in 'this time it's the real thing'.

clue.text: Stones left to tour Italy, Spain and Ireland

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all the way round it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: emeralds are precious stones
L is the abbreviation for left
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: The Rolling Stones set off on a tour of Italy, Spain and Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stones look like the band, but they are gems. EMERALDS and L together wrap round I, and E follows; 'and' links, and Ireland is the definition rather than a third country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emerald Isle is a poetic nickname for Ireland, from its green countryside.

clue.text: A poignant broadcast about a South American

indicators.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so these letters are scattered into a new order
about means around, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: the letters to rework
taken as written

explanation.surface: A moving radio or television programme about someone from South America.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of A POIGNANT wrap round the second A, which sits after PAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Patagonia is the southern tip of Argentina and Chile, so a native of it is a South American.

clue.text: Couple split over America changing direction ...

indicators.note: a thing laid over another covers it, so one piece wraps another
changing direction means heading back the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a rip is a split or tear
A is an abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A couple break up when one of them moves back to America; the dots lead on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: RIP goes round A to make RIAP, which then turns round. 'Split' looks like the verb for breaking up, but it is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is two people together, so it is a synonym for a romantic couple.

clue.text: ... at first expected Biden to welcome British decline

indicators.note: at first points to the start of words, so only their opening letters are used
welcoming a guest means taking them in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the first letters of these two words
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: Continuing the story, President Biden was expected to greet a fading Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots join this clue to the previous one for the surface only; the wordplay stands alone. Joe Biden was US president from 2021 to 2025.
explanation.definitionFit: To ebb is to recede like the tide, so it means to fall away or decline.

clue.text: Fat American soldier bachelor knocked up

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending letters up means reading them from the bottom, so they run backwards

blocks.note: a GI is a US army soldier
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a BA degree

explanation.surface: An overweight GI, a single man, has got a woman pregnant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked up' is British slang for making pregnant, a surface joke; in a down answer it turns the letters upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Big and fat are both used to describe a large, heavy build, so they are near synonyms.

clue.text: German inventor passes heads of English labs

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: to pass away is to die
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A German inventor walks past the directors of English laboratories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passes' reads as walking by, but it is the euphemism for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Diesel was the German engineer who invented the compression-ignition engine named after him.

clue.text: I squealed in an excited way, having got even

indicators.note: excited things jump about, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rework

explanation.surface: A fan shrieks with glee after their team scored the leveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got even' could suggest revenge, but here it is levelling a score.
explanation.definitionFit: To equalise is to level the score in a game, so a team that has done so has drawn level.

clue.text: Flipping trouble after lawyer husband makes bloomer

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it round, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: a DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor
H is the abbreviation for husband
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A lawyer's husband makes a blunder, and the trouble that follows is infuriating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British swear word and 'bloomer' as a blunder; in fact a bloomer is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A dahlia is a showy garden flower, and bloomer is crossword slang for any flowering plant.

clue.text: Flatulence can be a delightful thing

blocks.note: first meaning: wind in the gut
second meaning: great fun, as in 'it was a real laugh'

explanation.surface: A cheeky claim that breaking wind can be a pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: The informal sense, as in 'the party was a gas', is the one that makes the surface joke work.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both intestinal wind and, informally, something highly enjoyable or amusing.

clue.text: Thorny plant you start to lob at former husband

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: U is text-speak for you
the first letter of lob
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Someone is told to throw a prickly plant at their ex-husband.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a Latin genus name, so the wordplay is the way in; gorse is the common name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulex is the botanical genus name of gorse, a spiny yellow-flowered shrub.

clue.text: Crazy act in field saves old knight and private

indicators.note: something crazy is disordered, so these letters are rearranged
a keeper saves the ball by holding it, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: the letters to rework
O is the abbreviation for old
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A soldier does something mad on the battlefield and rescues an elderly knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like a soldier in the battle scene, but it is the adjective meaning secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Confidential information is kept secret and not shared, which is one sense of private.

clue.text: German river running through bluff in Owschlag

indicators.note: something running through words passes inside them across the join

blocks.note: found from the end of the first word into the start of the last

explanation.surface: A German river flows beneath a cliff near Owschlag, a village in northern Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is obscure, so the hidden letters do the work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Finow is a small river in Brandenburg, north-east Germany, a tributary of the Oder.

clue.text: New university (Dutch) that's exhibiting naked folk

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
U is the abbreviation for university
the Dutch word for 'that' is die

explanation.surface: A new Dutch university puts on a show of nude people.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed '(Dutch)' tells you to translate the next word into Dutch.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudie is informal for featuring nudity, as in a nudie magazine or film, so displaying unclothed people.

clue.text: For Kraftwerk, Yes and ZZ Top not top music!

indicators.note: 'not' here means without, so the named word is dropped

blocks.note: Kraftwerk are a German band, and ja is German for yes
the band's name with its second word taken away

explanation.surface: A list of rock bands, Kraftwerk, Yes and ZZ Top, all declared not the best music.
explanation.walkthrough: Yes and ZZ Top look like a third and fourth band; Kraftwerk being German signals that 'Yes' should be put into German.
explanation.definitionFit: Jazz is a genre of music, so the definition is a general category and the answer an example of it.

clue.text: Addicts right to have nothing to do with Buds

indicators.text: to have nothing to do with
indicators.note: having nothing to do with something means shutting it out, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: buds is American slang for pals
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Drug users are right to shun Budweiser beer, or perhaps cannabis buds.
explanation.walkthrough: Buds suggests beer or marijuana, but it means friends.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend is informal for a devotee or addict, as in a dope fiend or fitness fiend.

clue.text: Party time hosting retired teacher and old player

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw backwards, so the letters run the other way
a host has guests inside, so one piece contains another

a day is a period of time

explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests sport, but it is an actress: an old word for an actor is a player.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris Day was an American singer and film actress of the 1950s and 60s, so a player from the past.

clue.text: Rabbi and vicar swapping ecstasy for drop of ale

blocks.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a vicar's title

the first letter of ale

explanation.walkthrough: The E in REV is replaced by A.

clue.text: Just arrived in an insignificant place

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: present at this moment
second meaning: a place of no importance, as in 'the middle of it'

explanation.surface: A traveller has just turned up in some backwater.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning splits the answer into two words, 'now here'; the enumeration of one word hides that.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is used as a noun for an obscure, remote spot, and split in two it means someone has just come.

clue.text: Virginia Democrat meets Unionist unknown in capital

blocks.note: VA is the postal code for the US state of Virginia
D is the abbreviation for Democrat
U is the abbreviation for Unionist, as in Northern Irish politics
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: A Democrat from Virginia meets an anonymous Northern Irish Unionist in some capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Unionists in Northern Ireland want to stay part of the United Kingdom; the four abbreviations simply line up.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaduz is the capital city of Liechtenstein, the small principality between Switzerland and Austria.
